sections.heading: Signs Your Double Pane Windows Need Replacement
sections.body: Double pane windows rely on a sealed air or gas-filled cavity between two panes of glass to provide insulation and reduce noise transfer. Over time, the seal around that cavity can fail, allowing moisture to enter and creating the foggy or hazy appearance many property owners notice first. Beyond the visual issue, a broken seal means the insulating properties of the window are significantly diminished, making your HVAC system work harder to maintain a comfortable interior temperature. Other signs that replacement is warranted include visible condensation trapped between the panes, noticeable drafts near window frames, difficulty opening or closing the sash, and chips or cracks in the glass itself. If your Ashburn property is experiencing any of these symptoms, waiting too long can lead to further frame damage or interior moisture problems. Our team can assess the condition of your units and recommend whether a full double pane replacement or an insulated glass unit swap is the right course of action for your specific situation.

sections.heading: Our Double Pane Replacement Process in Ashburn
sections.body: We keep our replacement process straightforward and transparent so you always know what to expect. After an initial assessment of your windows, we measure each opening precisely and source insulated glass units that match the specifications of your existing frames whenever possible. Proper measurement is critical — even small discrepancies can lead to poor seals, air infiltration, or glass movement over time. Our glaziers remove the failed unit carefully, clean the frame channels, and install the new double pane glass with appropriate glazing compounds and setting blocks to ensure a secure, weathertight fit. We serve properties across Ashburn, from commercial office buildings and retail centers near Loudoun Station to single-family homes in established neighborhoods. Every job is completed with attention to detail, and we clean up the work area before we leave so you can get back to normal operations with minimal disruption.

faq.q: Can you replace just the glass in my double pane window without replacing the entire frame?
faq.a: In many cases, yes. If your window frame is structurally sound and undamaged, we can often replace only the insulated glass unit inside it. This is typically a more practical approach when the frame itself is in good condition. We will assess your windows and let you know which option makes sense for your specific situation.

faq.q: What causes double pane windows to fail and fog up?
faq.a: The most common cause is seal failure around the perimeter of the insulated glass unit. Once the seal breaks down, outside air and moisture can enter the space between the panes, causing the foggy or hazy appearance. Seal failure can result from age, temperature cycling, physical damage, or improper original installation. Replacing the failed unit is the only reliable fix — cleaning the inside of the glass is not possible without full replacement.
